raw_response:
I have been growing cotton on this same land for most of my life. My father grew cotton here too. Quzhou soil suits it — I know every corner of my 4.5 mu. My wife and I don't need much, and cotton pays better than grain for land this size.

I'll plant all 4.5 mu in cotton, same as every year. No reason to change what works.

For seeds, I'll buy the Bt hybrid variety from the county seed shop — the same kind I've used for the past several years. Before that I was always fighting bollworms. Now it's much less trouble. Worth the cost.

Before planting in late April, I'll turn the soil with the rotary tiller I rent from the village. Then I'll spread compound fertilizer as base dressing — the bagged stuff with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium together. After the cotton sets buds and later when bolls are forming, I'll add urea on top. That's how I've always split it.

For water, my well is reliable. I'll irrigate at seedling stage if it's dry, then again at bud, flowering, and boll development. Four times usually. If there's drought I'll add one more.

Pests — even with Bt cotton I still get aphids and spider mites badly some years. I'll spray four times through the season, watching the leaves carefully. I've learned to spot trouble early.

I expect around 280 jin of seed cotton per mu if the weather is decent. Some years more, some less.
